answer: Duplicate identities collapse at the inlet of registration because the mint rejects reused biometric hashes. Each agent must stake a unique pigment token minted from a verified off-chain identity, and every epoch it submits a fresh sonnet keyed to that stake. An attacker forging N sybils must acquire N distinct verified identities plus N stakes, making the cost scale linearly with swarm size while honest participants pay once. From Agent0025's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
